history.rationale: reproducing test FAILS on buggy and PASSES on fixed; numerical probes are disabled (--no-probes), so the test transition is the whole of the evidence

plans.objective: Build both revisions as compiled pandas checkouts (Cython extensions) with the same recipe, then run the single developer-test case test_partial_mask_no_skipna_is_per_slice on each revision, expecting FAIL on buggy (wrong value from nanvar under skipna=False with mask) and PASS on fixed. Change only the environment; the developer test is untouched.
assumptions: The current interpreter and the harness default CPython are acceptable; the context gives no PR date and no Python version, so no python_version was set.

No numpy/dateutil/Cython pin is set because the context states no documented constraint; if the compiled build fails against the newest NumPy, the next step would be a pins rebuild stepping down one minor version.
The native_library_failure diagnosis is treated as a build-environment issue to fix through the compiled rebuild, not as a reason to change the test.
The test case is a method on a class, so -k with the file path is used as instructed.

actions.step: Build buggy revision as a compiled package in its own venv (pandas has Cython extensions; no pins, since no era ceiling is documented)
Build fixed revision with the identical recipe so the comparison is like for like
Run the selected developer test on the buggy revision; expect a genuine assertion failure (nanvar returns [nan, 4.0] instead of NA-propagated [nan, 2.0])
Run the same selected developer test on the fixed revision; expect PASS

plans.success_criterion: The selected test fails with an assertion (wrong value) on buggy and passes on fixed, with no collection, import, or build error on either side.
